advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS suppression line-scoped (or occurrence-count-scoped) so an exception cannot blanket newly-added below-seam reads of the same symbol in the file.
evidence: _exception_pairs(): `return {(str(e["path"]), str(e["symbol"])) for e in LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS}` — no lineno component
_suppressed(): `if (relpath, symbol) in pairs: return True` suppresses by (path, symbol) regardless of acc.lineno

Rationale strings document specific lines (e.g. `"_jira_onboard.py L63/191: legacy dynamic env read (os.environ.get)."`) but the (path, 'os.environ.get') pair blankets all os.environ.get calls in that file
Symbols like `os.environ.get`, `os.environ[...]`, and `load_config` recur many times per file, so one exception row covers unbounded future reads of the same shape
`def _parse(path): try: return ast.parse(...) except (OSError, SyntaxError, ValueError): return None`
_scan_files: `tree = _parse(py); if tree is None: continue` — file skipped, no error recorded

_check_registry_completeness: same `if tree is None: continue`, so a credential boundary that fails to parse silently drops its reads from read_names, potentially masking or falsely triggering completeness
advisory.finding: LEGACY_EXCEPTIONS suppression is keyed on (path, symbol) with no line number, so a single recorded exception silences EVERY occurrence of that symbol in the file — including below-seam reads added after the exception was recorded. This is a fail-open window in the gate: a new os.environ.get / credential / env read introduced into an already-excepted module passes silently.
merged_from: _parse() swallows all parse errors and returns None; _scan_files, _check_registry_completeness, and derive_backend_keys then silently `continue`, so any module that fails to parse is entirely skipped by the ownership gate — a fail-open path where an unparseable file evades all below-seam classification.
scenarios: A developer adds a new os.environ.get('NEW_KNOB') to _cli/_jira_onboard.py; the existing ('_cli/_jira_onboard.py','os.environ.get') exception suppresses it with no gate failure
A new credential env read added to a module already excepted for that credential symbol passes silently
advisory.suggested_fix: Include the documented lineno(s) in the exception key/tuple and match acc.lineno against them in _suppressed, so only the specific recorded read is suppressed.
